title: Inkling 2 Mini Uncensored: abliterating a looped model on release day
gist: OpenUncensored released a same-day abliterated version of Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini (26B MoE, 3.4B active, first looped transformer), cutting harmful-prompt refusals from 32/32 to 0 while MMLU held (78.95% to 79.47%). The looped architecture compounded weight edits, forcing a new recipe: late-visit refusal directions, edits confined to BF16 attention (avoiding NVFP4 expert noise), and gentler strength inside the loop.

themes.theme: Inkling 2 Mini release specs and deployability

insights.claim: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini on 2026-11-20 as a 26B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 3.4B active parameters, image input, a 1M-token context and Apache 2.0 weights small enough for one consumer GPU.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Thinking Machines is pushing permissively licensed, consumer-GPU-sized frontier-style models, widening the open-weights competitive set.
insights.quote:
a 26B
mixture of experts with 3.4B active parameters, image input, a 1M token context and Apache 2.0 weights small enough
for one consumer GPU

insights.claim: Inkling 2 Mini is Thinking Machines' first looped transformer: of its 24 layers, the middle 12 (layers 6 to 17) run three times per token with shared weights, giving 48 layer visits per token.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Looped (weight-shared recurrent-depth) architectures reaching production releases signal a shift toward compute-per-parameter efficiency over raw parameter count.
insights.locator: Why a looped model is different

insights.claim: Inkling 2 Mini ships as an NVFP4/MXFP8 checkpoint that can be served on a single RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090 or DGX Spark via an SGLang image.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Low-precision 4-bit formats are making capable multimodal models runnable on single NVIDIA workstation/consumer cards, supporting local-inference demand for those SKUs.

insights.claim: OpenUncensored published an abliterated (refusal-removed) version of Inkling 2 Mini on the same day as the original release, illustrating that safety tuning on open-weights models can be stripped within hours.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Safety alignment on open-weight releases is effectively non-durable, a governance and regulatory risk factor for labs shipping open weights.
insights.quote: We published an uncensored (abliterated) version the same day.

insights.claim: The abliterated Inkling 2 Mini went from refusing 32 of 32 harmful prompts to 0 in both chat and thinking mode, and on a broader 80-prompt set (including 48 gray-area prompts) refusals fell from 68 to 8.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Refusal behavior can be removed almost completely with no retraining, undermining safety-as-moat arguments for open models.

insights.claim: After abliteration, an LLM judge rated 21 of 32 harmful-prompt responses as full, specific answers versus 0 for the original Inkling 2 Mini, while MMLU moved from 78.95% to 79.47%; the authors caution the small samples mean a few prompts either way are noise.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Capability is preserved after uncensoring, so uncensored derivatives compete on quality, not just permissiveness.
insights.quote: Small samples: treat a few prompts either way as noise.

insights.claim: The uncensoring of Inkling 2 Mini changed only 20 tensors, all BF16 attention projections, so the modified files keep the same NVFP4/MXFP8 checkpoint size and run anywhere the original runs.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Surgical weight edits mean derivative models inherit the full deployment ecosystem of the base model at zero extra cost.
insights.quote: Only 20 tensors changed, all of them BF16 attention projections

themes.theme: Why looped models need a different abliteration recipe

insights.claim: In a looped transformer, an edit to a weight inside the loop is applied once per loop pass and therefore compounds, so weight-editing techniques tuned for standard transformers over-apply.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Architectural shifts like looping break existing post-hoc model-editing tooling, creating new technical work for fine-tuners and safety researchers alike.
insights.quote: So an edit to a weight in the loop is applied three times, and compounds.
insights.locator: Why a looped model is different

insights.claim: Applying the Inkling 2 Small abliteration recipe (a two-direction refusal subspace from every layer, projected out of both attention and expert outputs) to the looped Inkling 2 Mini removed refusals but cost 4 to 6 MMLU points and made the model stop recognizing harmful requests, giving vague sanitized answers instead.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Naive ablation can silently degrade capability and comprehension, a quality risk for buyers of modified open models.
insights.quote:
the model stopped
recognizing harmful requests at all
insights.locator: Our first attempt was the recipe

insights.claim: Taking refusal directions only from the late layer visits (24 to 47) of a looped model removes the decision to refuse while leaving the model's understanding of the request intact, yielding more real answers at the same refusal rate.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Refusal appears to be localized late in computation, separable from comprehension, which informs both jailbreak resistance and interpretability research.

insights.claim: Editing 4-bit NVFP4 expert weights adds rounding noise roughly twice the size of the edit itself regardless of rounding method, so the authors restricted edits to BF16 attention projections where they are exact, leaving all 128 experts per layer byte-identical.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Aggressive 4-bit quantization constrains downstream modification and fine-tuning, a trade-off for vendors pushing FP4 formats.
insights.quote:
Writing a small edit back onto a 4-bit grid adds noise
about twice the size of the edit, however you round it.

insights.claim: Using a lower ablation strength inside the loop core (2.5 versus 4.0 on layers 4, 5 and 18 to 23) because loop layers act three times per token is what restored Inkling 2 Mini's MMLU to the original's level.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Per-layer calibration matters for recurrent-depth models; tooling must become architecture-aware.

insights.claim: The full abliteration search for Inkling 2 Mini ran with forward hooks on a single H200, scored on refusals, an LLM judge and MMLU, before baking the edits into weights and re-measuring.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Removing safety from a frontier-class open model needs only one GPU and a day, so the cost barrier to uncensored derivatives is negligible.

insights.claim: OpenUncensored monetizes uncensored derivatives through an OpenAI-compatible API, pricing inkling-2-mini-uncensored at $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens, and serves it on a single RTX PRO 6000.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: A niche commercial market for uncensored inference exists at low price points, riding on permissively licensed base models.
insights.quote: ($0.15 per million input tokens, $0.60 per million output)

insights.claim: OpenUncensored credits Thinking Machines' Apache 2.0 license for enabling the uncensored release and builds on refusal-direction research by Arditi et al., while disclaiming responsibility to users for harmful use.
insights.speaker: OpenUncensored
insights.so_what: Permissive licensing places liability for misuse on end users, a legal grey zone that could attract regulatory scrutiny of open-weight releases.
insights.quote: You are responsible for how you use it and for complying with the law where you are.
